Generate a U-shaped profile by subtracting an offset rectangular box from a larger one, ensuring both ends remain open. The larger box should measure 450 mm in length, 70 mm in width, and 40 mm in height. Subtract an inner box that is 60 mm wide and 35 mm and high with same 450mm length, maintain a wall thickness of 5 mm around the sides and base, resulting in a U-shape, open at the top and sides | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan (no function execution yet)

1. Establish the outer prism  
   • Use functions.block once with subtraction = False  
   • Dimensions: x_size = 450 mm, y_size = 70 mm, z_size = 40 mm  
   • Basepoint: x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 (object extends positively from the origin)

2. Carve out the inner solid to create the U-shape  
   • Call functions.block a second time with subtraction = True  
   • Dimensions: x_size = 450 mm, y_size = 60 mm, z_size = 35 mm  
   • Basepoint: x = 0, y = 5 mm, z = 5 mm  
     – This gives 5 mm side-wall thickness (70 – 60 = 10 → 5 mm each side)  
     – 5 mm bottom thickness (40 – 35 = 5 mm)  
   • Because the inner block has the same 450 mm length as the outer one, the front and back faces are completely removed, leaving both ends open.  
   • The 35 mm inner height stops 5 mm below the top, so the top stays fully open.

3. Optionally close the sequence with a single functions.finished call, confirming that all required geometry calls have been made.

This two-block sequence yields the requested U-profile: walls and base 5 mm thick, open at the top and at both ends, produced solely through the described function calls.
